awd_titl_txt: CHAI - Strengthening Cyber Infrastructure for Enhanced STEM Education and Research at TMCC
awd_abstract_narration:
A goal of the Tribal Colleges and Universities Program (TCUP) is to increase the science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) instructional and research capacities of specific institutions of higher education that serve the Nation's indigenous students. Expanding the instructional, research, and development capacity at these institutions expands the opportunities for students to pursue challenging, rewarding careers in STEM fields, provides for research studies in areas that may be locally relevant, and encourages a faculty community to look beyond the traditional classroom for intellectual and professional growth. This project aligns directly with that goal by strengthening the STEM cyberinfrastructure for instructional and research activities. The project aims to enhance cyberinfrastructure and cybersecurity necessary to facilitate development of the institution in STEM fields and for the protection of sensitive data. 

The project upgrades specific STEM IT resources at the institution to improve the resiliency and security of STEM operations, data management, teaching, and research enterprises. Improvements to Turtle Mountain Community College’s (TMCC’s) network and cybersecurity foster the college’s ability to implement advances in STEM instruction and research. The activities for developing STEM cyberinfrastructure directly support current and future projects, including the revitalization of the Ojibway language.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
This project strengthened the digital infrastructure and cybersecurity capabilities at the college in order to support teaching, learning, and research in a safe and reliable technology environment. With support from the National Science Foundation, the project focused on three key areas: improving network performance, strengthening cybersecurity risk management, and enhancing identity and password security for students, faculty, and staff.

First, the project significantly improved the campus network and wireless infrastructure. As modern education increasingly relies on online platforms, cloud systems, and digital learning tools, reliable high-speed internet access is essential. To address growing demand for faster and more secure wireless connectivity, the college upgraded its network switches, wireless access points, and firewalls. These upgrades support modern Wi-Fi standards, including Wi-Fi 6E, which can deliver significantly faster speeds and better performance for large numbers of users. Research has consistently shown that reliable Wi-Fi access is one of the most important technologies for students’ academic success. By modernizing the campus network infrastructure, the project improved network performance, increased reliability, and strengthened security protections for everyone who uses the college’s systems.

Second, the project implemented a comprehensive cybersecurity risk management and compliance framework to better protect institutional data and digital systems. Colleges and universities face increasing cybersecurity threats, including attempts to access sensitive data, disrupt operations, or exploit system vulnerabilities. To address these risks, the college adopted a modern risk management platform and engaged cybersecurity experts to conduct a vulnerability assessment and penetration test. These tests simulate potential cyberattacks to identify weaknesses before they can be exploited. The assessment identified several minor vulnerabilities, which were quickly addressed to improve overall security.

The project also implemented a compliance and risk management platform to help the college continuously monitor cybersecurity risks, manage policies, and maintain alignment with regulatory and industry standards. This system helps the institution identify potential threats early, respond more quickly to security issues, and maintain a strong security posture over time. Policies supporting cybersecurity and data protection are currently being finalized and integrated into the system to ensure that faculty and staff understand and follow best practices for protecting institutional information.

Third, the project strengthened identity management and password security across campus. Weak or reused passwords remain one of the most common causes of cybersecurity breaches. To address this challenge, the college implemented a secure password management system for faculty, staff, and students. This platform allows users to store login credentials safely while encouraging stronger password practices. The system improves authentication security and reduces the likelihood of unauthorized access to sensitive systems or information.

In addition, the college began implementing secure identity federation services that allow students and faculty to access educational and research resources more easily across participating institutions. These services support collaboration, resource sharing, and improved access to academic tools used in higher education and research.

Beyond technology improvements, the project also supported long-term cybersecurity education and awareness. Faculty and staff received training on password security and cybersecurity best practices, and new policies were introduced to strengthen institutional security practices. External cybersecurity consultants were also engaged to help develop vulnerability testing approaches that could involve student participation in the future, creating opportunities for experiential learning in cybersecurity.

Overall, the project achieved all of its original goals. The college successfully upgraded its network infrastructure, implemented a cybersecurity risk management framework, improved password and identity security, and strengthened its ability to protect institutional data and systems. These improvements enhance the reliability and safety of the college’s technology environment for students, employees, and the broader community.

The outcomes of this project contribute to both the intellectual merit and broader impacts of the work supported by the National Science Foundation. From a research and technical perspective, the project demonstrates how smaller and rural institutions can implement modern cybersecurity frameworks and infrastructure to support secure digital learning environments. From a broader impact perspective, the project improves access to reliable technology, protects sensitive information, and creates a more secure foundation for education, research, and collaboration. By strengthening the institution’s digital infrastructure and cybersecurity practices, the project helps ensure that students and faculty have safe, dependable access to the tools and resources they need to succeed in today’s technology-driven educational environment.
